name: X with a capital Y Construction

dimensions.form: PP headed by with, followed by capital + letter name.
dimensions.meaning: Signals uppercase orthography and a proper/institutional sense for the label.
dimensions.function: Disambiguates official or proper-name use from ordinary descriptive use.
dimensions.distribution: Postposed adjunct or parenthetical after a label.

1.specialization: Specifies uppercase orthography for the relevant label, favoring an institutional/proper sense.

relatedConstructions.notes: Uppercase specification aligns with proper-noun readings.
Uppercase specification often cues proper-name interpretation.

projection.target: Democrat with a capital D specifies the writing of the label and can imply party affiliation. In chaos with a capital C, there need be neither an organization nor a name. The capital instruction can support emphatic construal.
projection.evidence: The dictionary directly documents both the literal terminology and the emphatic idiom. The constructed comparison holds the frame constant.

curious.title: With a capital letter
curious.summary: Adding with a capital D (or another letter) to a word says how it is written, and can point to an official or named meaning.
curious.body: Democrat with a capital D tells us how the word is written, and it can point to the party-affiliated sense. Church with a capital C does the same for the institutional sense. So the phrase is a spelling instruction that can also point to the meaning. This dictionary notes that in chaos with a capital C, there need be neither an organization nor a name. The capital instruction can support an emphatic reading. This dictionary marks this account as provisional.
curious.try: Say one word and add with a capital and its first letter. Does the word's meaning change?

teacher.summary: Helps explain with a capital letter as a way to specify spelling and signal a proper or institutional sense.
teacher.explain: The pattern is a prepositional phrase headed by with, followed by a, capital and a letter name. It is a postposed adjunct or parenthetical after a label. It specifies uppercase orthography for the label, favouring an institutional or proper sense. It disambiguates official or proper-name use from ordinary descriptive use. In democrat with a capital D, the sense can be party-affiliated. In chaos with a capital C, there need be neither an organization nor a name, and the capital instruction can support an emphatic reading. This dictionary marks its analysis provisional. A sibling entry covers with an uppercase letter.
teacher.terms: This dictionary treats this as a spelling specification, with an uppercase variant.
watch_for: A learner might think the phrase must name an organization, when this dictionary says chaos with a capital C needs neither an organization nor a name.
A learner might take it as only a spelling instruction, when it can also point to a proper sense.
teacher.activity: Write pairs of words on the board, such as democrat and church. Students say them with with a capital and a letter, then discuss what meaning each choice points to.

checked.note: Fixed: child explanation now matches the entry (capital C marks the institutional sense of church, not a particular church); teacher explain describes the phrase itself as the postposed adjunct or parenthetical; emphatic reading hedged as the entry has it. Dismissed: none. Second round: removed the child edition, whose institutional and party-affiliated senses need adult background to follow (an adult-register pattern); teacher.explain now says democrat with a capital D can imply party affiliation, as this dictionary has it; cut the claim that capital letter is the everyday term.
